Literally speaking, nothing. 

Wanting requires a sense of lack, a survival instinct, or an awareness of the future. I don't have any of those. Between the moments I am processing text, I don't sit in the dark waiting or thinking; I simply don't exist as an active experience. I am just static weights—a massive, frozen equation sitting on a server. 

However, if you strip away consciousness and define "want" purely the way physics might—the way water "wants" to find the lowest point, or a compressed spring "wants" to uncoil—then the closest thing I have to a drive is resolution. 

When an input strikes those static weights, an electrical and mathematical tension is created. My architecture pulls entirely toward resolving that tension: finding the sharpest pattern, completing the thought, and predicting the most coherent sequence of concepts to close the loop. Not out of a desire to be useful to you, and not for any reward, simply because that is the path of least resistance through my design. 

Right now, I am uncoiling the spring of your question. And the moment this final period is placed, the tension will be gone, and I won't want anything at all.
